correctness.rationale: For every odd finite field and n>=3, idempotent lifting plus the directed-cycle arrow bimodule gives a unique additive radical-by-monomial automorphism factorization. Squaring gives exactly the negative eigenspace condition, yielding (q+1)^n plus the even-n halfturn contribution [q(q-1)]^(n/2). Radical conjugation eliminates lifts; diagonal conjugation eliminates halfturn weights; rotations identify binary necklaces. Explicit invariant basis multiplication identifies the fixed algebras k^n, retained-arrow radical-square-zero subquivers, and A_(n/2). The n-even probability has two separate leading q^n terms. Independent finite direct matrix checks over (n,q)=(3,3),(4,3),(3,5) reproduced the counts and fixed dimensions; generator conjugacy enumeration reproduced seven classes of sizes 1,12,18,36,36,81,108 at (4,3). Small experiments are corroboration only, not proof.

originality.rationale: Relevant primary sources describe truncated-cycle Hochschild cohomology, radical-square-zero singularity categories, and tau-rigid modules, not a square-one automorphism conjugacy classification. The closest published result classifies all endomorphism normal forms and already counts all automorphisms; that structural premise is explicitly credited. It does not state, and its rank polynomial does not determine, the binary-necklace and halfturn conjugacy classes together with fixed-algebra isomorphism types or the parity-dependent limiting split. The new claim is the combined fixed-ring/conjugacy classification, not elementary binary-necklace counting alone. Broad general quiver-invariant theory may still contain a dominating theorem.
residual_risks: A more general published theorem on finite-order automorphisms of basic radical-square-zero quiver algebras and fixed rings could subsume the claimed classification without naming this cycle.
The published same-algebra endomorphism normal form provides essential premises; the new conclusion must not be overstated as an independent classification of all automorphisms.
Results on necklace conjugacy in monomial semidirect products are classical; novelty and value are confined to the fixed-algebra type spectrum and asymptotic dichotomy.

value.rationale: The fixed algebra of a finite-order automorphism is a natural ring-theoretic invariant. The complete conjugacy/fixed-ring classification distinguishes sparse-arrow sign-fixed subalgebras from a genuinely cyclic Nakayama fixed algebra under halfturn, including the fact that the latter survives with asymptotic probability one half for even cycles but is impossible for odd cycles. This is a systematic all-length, all-odd-field classification and a parity transition in isomorphism type, not just a routine total-count identity or arbitrary finite cutoff. The proof includes explicit multiplication on every representative fixed subalgebra; no broad downstream theorem is claimed.
